order.statement: Hiragana before katakana, gojuon order, in groups of five, then dakuten and handakuten, then yoon, then small tsu and long vowels, then the three particles, then katakana as a re-skin, then the extended digraphs.
verified: japanese-study-structure.md section D: hiragana before katakana, verified across Tofugu, Genki and Tae Kim; the one dissent is the immersion camp, which teaches kana beside listening rather than the two scripts together
japanese-study-structure.md section D: gojuon order in groups of five, verified against Tofugu
japanese-study-structure.md section D: dakuten and handakuten first, then yoon, then small tsu last, verified against Tofugu
japanese-phonology-kana.md section D8: MEXT groups the writing-system items as steps 1 to 5
ours: japanese-phonology-kana.md section D8 states that the step boundaries and the unlocks column are the researcher's, not a source's

japanese-study-structure.md section D states that keeping gojuon rather than frequency order is the researcher's reasoning: dakuten, yoon and romanisation are column rules, so column order is the rule-teaching order
japanese-study-structure.md section D: reading is the product and writing is an opt-in track is the researcher's call, because a browser cannot grade a stroke
unresolved: japanese-phonology-kana.md section F: no controlled comparison of hiragana-first against katakana-first or simultaneous teaching was found. Treat the order as settled convention, not a demonstrated result.

steps.content: 46 basic hiragana, gojūon order, in 5-character rows
steps.unlocks: reading any hiragana word aloud, even one you do not know
most native vocabulary; the full sound inventory

steps.content: yōon, small tsu, hiragana long vowels (おう vs おお, えい)
steps.unlocks: correct beat counting; きょう against きよう

steps.content: the three particles は へ を
steps.unlocks: reading a real sentence rather than a word list

steps.content: 46 basic katakana, same order, taught as a re-skin of step 1
steps.unlocks: writing your own name, and reading a menu

steps.content: katakana dakuten, yōon, ー, ッ
steps.unlocks: ordinary loanwords: メニュー, コーヒー, サッカー

steps.content: the extended digraphs (ティ ファ ウィ ヴ シェ ジェ チェ) plus section B
steps.unlocks: converting an unknown English word yourself, which is the game

confusables_note: The confusable pairs are taught as contrasts rather than in isolation. They live beside the rows they belong to, in hiragana.json and katakana.json.
